neighboring_unit_entries.title: LeClair's thermodynamic zero-free argument depends on its decisive assumption
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: A scattering-kernel formalism makes physical thermodynamic quantities finite in a strip and argues that an off-line zero would violate an assumed interaction effect; the source explicitly identifies that assumption as why the claimed RH conclusion is not a proof.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Prime-factor walks yield an Erdős-Kac Gaussian limit
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Mapping distinct-prime-factor counts to a corrected random walk transfers Brownian/central-limit intuition into a limiting distribution for an arithmetic function.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Quadratic forms, unique prime factorization, Möbius inversion, Dirichlet convolution, integer partitions, and prime-factor counts admit physical representations as lattice energies, many-body states, gas mixtures, fluctuations, and random walks.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: Several systems are fictitious, ensemble choice changes predictions, generalized zeta analogies can fail, and probabilistic resemblance or a failed sufficient criterion does not settle RH.
